description: Agent Support Operations: submit support tickets with the queue record they belong to: the queue with its reference, name, the moment it is read at, the open limit in hours it states and the channels it takes tickets from; each ticket with its id, reference, channel, customer, issue, the moment it was opened, its status (open, pending, solved or closed), the moment it was solved or closed, the moment of the first response to the customer, the moment the customer last wrote, what the customer’s last message says (the issue is still open or it is resolved) and the tickets it is linked to. The signed report gives the queue and the tickets, each closed ticket against the response recorded before it closed, each customer’s tickets for one issue across channels against the links between them, each open ticket’s age at the reading against the open limit, and each ticket’s status against the customer’s last message, and counts them, and names divergent support tickets: a ticket closed with no response recorded, the same issue opened as separate tickets across channels with no link, a ticket open past the limit the queue states, and a ticket status that contradicts the customer’s last message, solved or closed while the customer wrote after the close or says the issue is still open; then a ticket from a channel the queue does not list and a ticket left open after the customer says the issue is resolved, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No tickets, no reading moment or no open limit beside open tickets, or an open ticket with no opening time to the minute leaves those points unverified. Channels and customers match without case or punctuation, issues by their words with plurals folded, linked tickets by letters and digits, and ages count in hours between two moments that carry a time. This reads whether the support tickets hold together with the queue record they belong to, ticket by ticket. Verdict support_ticket_divergent, support_ticket_partial, support_ticket_unverified or support_ticket_consistent. POST /api/support-ticket-check. Reads the support records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it answers no customer, sends no message and opens, closes or changes no ticket, which stay with the support team, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Support Operations reads support operation records: ticket logs, first response records, resolution records, escalation records, promise records, performance records, backlog records and the support summary, each against the queue record, the stated response commitments, the customer confirmations, the stated escalation triggers, what the records show happened, the stated service commitments, the ticket list or the records beneath it. The family’s ground is support work already done, read across the whole queue: the DiligenceOps support brief reads one support conversation and lists the promises made in it, and the Agent Feedback family reads the loop around feedback on work, while this family checks whether the support operation’s records hold together across tickets. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-support-operations-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-support-operations/.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

as_of.description: The moment the queue is read at, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

channels.description: The channels the queue takes tickets from.

open_limit_hours.description: The longest a ticket may stay open, in hours, as the queue record states it.

tickets.description: Each support ticket in the queue.

channel.description: The support channel, such as email, chat or phone.

closed_at.description: When the ticket was solved or closed, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

customer.description: The customer name or reference as the record writes it.

first_response_at.description: When the first response to the customer was recorded, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

issue.description: The issue as the record names it.

last_customer_at.description: When the customer last wrote, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

last_customer_state.description: What the customer’s last message says: the issue is still open or it is resolved.

linked.description: The other tickets this ticket is linked to.

opened_at.description: When the ticket was opened, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

status.description: The ticket status: open, pending, solved or closed.

name: wever_support-ticket-check
title: Support ticket check
